paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Solomon built cities, forts, store cities and chariot cities, and the passage still says the work of the LORD's house was carried out and completed (2 Chronicles 8:16). Big projects are not the problem. The question is what sits in the middle of the day, and for Solomon it was worship. He offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and he kept the daily requirement 'according to the commandment of Moses' (2 Chronicles 8:12-13).

Look at HOW he did it, because that part is for you and me. He set up the priests, Levites and gatekeepers 'in keeping with the ordinances of his father David,' and the text says they 'did not turn aside from the king's command' in any matter (2 Chronicles 8:14-15). Solomon didn't invent a new way to honor God. He followed the way that was already given. I think that's the quiet wisdom here: when your plate is FULL, you don't need a fancier plan, you need a faithful one.

Even his home shows it. Solomon said that the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy (2 Chronicles 8:11), so he treated holy things as holy. I think that's a good question to carry into your own busy week, baker. What in your day is holy ground, and are you guarding it? Keep that first, and the rest has a way of getting built.
